html:
SMTO-CMP-0027 — This task is stopping, so it can't be marked finished

GUID: b770bb67-cd70-482d-8e4f-f1410f6da3b6
Slug: completion-run-stopping
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • This task was asked to stop, by the Stop button or by reaching its time limit, just as the AI tried to finish or start more commands. SMTO didn't accept the finish or start those commands.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait until the task no longer shows Stopping… and its status changes to Stopped or Partial · resumable. Steps that were already running need to settle before SMTO can say where the task ended.
  2. Expand the task and check which steps completed, so you know which changes already happened. The stop may have come partway through, so some changes may be done and others not.
  3. If you still want the rest done, select Continue task or Resume if shown, or send a new message describing only what's left. Work from before the stop is kept, and naming only what's left avoids repeating finished changes.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Stopped or Partial · resumable, and if you continued it, the new attempt finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. If the task stays stuck on Stopping…, open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Restart task until you know which changes already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Direct completion or shell-sequence admission was refused because a Stop (cancellation) request, a steering interrupt or the run's wall-clock deadline was already active for the run.

What this means

  • Cancellation/Stop ownership checks detect an active stop request before direct completion or sequence admission. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Cancellation/Stop ownership checks detect an active stop request before direct completion or sequence admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the durable Stop transition and settling operations before another control request.

How to fix it

  • Check the run's cancel_requested/stop state and events for the pending Stop or the budget.wall_clock deadline. Let the Stop transition settle and inspect the durable receipts of operations that were already running before using Continue task, Resume or Restart task; do not replay mutations whose outcome is not yet recorded.
  • Wait for the current stop transition and inspect durable state before another action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported stop settlement establishes the original work state before any later continuation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
